# Croup

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Pediatrics > Pediatric ENT and pulmonology > Croup*

[Original Article Link](/library/n407PT)

---

## Summary

Viral croup (i.e., acute laryngotracheobronchitis) is an inflammation of the <u>upper airway</u> that occurs in young children. It is most often caused by the <u>parainfluenza virus</u>. This condition is characterized by a barking <u>cough</u>, hoarse voice, and <u>inspiratory stridor</u>, all of which often worsen at night. More severe symptoms are associated with higher degrees of <u>airway obstruction</u> and include <u>signs of respiratory distress</u>, which can rarely progress to <u>respiratory failure</u>. Croup is primarily a <u>clinical diagnosis</u>, and diagnostic studies are only performed for severe disease, diagnostic uncertainty, or recurrent episodes of croup. All patients with viral croup should receive <u>glucocorticoids</u> (preferably <u>dexamethasone</u>) and supportive treatment. Patients with moderate or <u>severe croup</u> should also be evaluated for admission and receive <u>nebulized</u> <u>racemic epinephrine</u> and <u>supplemental oxygen</u>. The prognosis of uncomplicated croup is good, and complete recovery typically occurs within seven days of onset.

## Epidemiology

* Peak <u>incidence</u>: 6 months to 3 years

* Most common in fall and winter





References:[[1]](/library/2daT6j)




Epidemiological data refers to the US, unless otherwise specified.

---

## Etiology

* Most common <u>pathogen</u>: <u>parainfluenza viruses</u> (75% of cases) [[2]](/library/n717mR0)

* Other pathogens: <u>respiratory syncytial virus</u> (<u>RSV</u>), <u>adenovirus</u>, <u>influenza virus</u>, <u>SARS-CoV-2</u> (<u>COVID-19</u>) [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[4]](/library/M71MmR0)

---

## Pathophysiology

* Important membrane-bound <u>virulence factors</u> of <u>parainfluenza virus</u> include: 

* <u>Hemagglutinin</u>: binds <u>sialic acid</u> → viral entry

* <u>Neuraminidase</u>: release and spread of <u>virions</u>

* Viral infection → inflammation of the <u>upper airway</u> with <u>edema</u> formation and infiltration of inflammatory cells → narrowing of <u>subglottic</u> <u>airway</u> (<u>inspiratory stridor</u>) and <u>increased work of breathing</u>

---

## Clinical features

* <u>Prodromal</u> phase: 1–2 days of <u>upper respiratory tract infection</u> symptoms (<u>rhinitis</u>, low-grade <u>fever</u>, <u>sore throat</u>) [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[5]](/library/_715oR0)

* <u>Symptoms of croup</u> ; last 2–7 days and typically manifest in the late evening/night. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)

* Characteristic features include seal-like barking <u>cough</u>, <u>hoarseness</u>, and <u>inspiratory stridor</u> due to <u>subglottic</u> narrowing. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[5]](/library/_715oR0)

* Mild croup: <u>Stridor</u> may be absent or only manifest in <u>agitated</u> individuals.

* Moderate croup

* <u>Stridor</u> and <u>dyspnea</u> may be present at rest.

* Thoracic <u>retractions</u> are typically visible.

* Affected individuals may be <u>tachycardic</u> or <u>tachypneic</u>.

* Severe croup

* Severe <u>stridor</u> and <u>dyspnea</u> are present at rest.

* Air entry is decreased.

* <u>Hypoxemia</u>, an <u>altered mental state</u>, and/or other <u>signs of impending respiratory failure</u> may be present.

* <u>Upper airway</u> obstruction can cause <u>pulsus paradoxus</u>. [[6]](/library/kH1mqR0)

* <u>Agitation</u> can worsen symptoms and precipitate complete <u>airway obstruction</u>.





> [!WARNING]
> Do not examine the throat of a child with significant <u>stridor</u> because the resulting <u>agitation</u> may precipitate complete <u>airway obstruction</u>. [[7]](/library/w71hLR0)

## Diagnosis

### General principles [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[10]](/library/MybMfw)[[11]](/library/Od1IJf0)




* Croup is most commonly diagnosed based on the presence of characteristic <u>clinical features of croup</u>.

* Diagnostic studies are not routinely required; do not delay treatment in unstable patients to obtain studies.

* Indications for diagnostic studies include:

* Atypical presentation or diagnostic uncertainty, to rule out <u>differential diagnoses of stridor</u>

* Severe disease

* Recurrent episodes of croup





> [!WARNING]
> Do not delay treatment of <u>stridor</u> to perform diagnostic studies.




### Imaging




* <u>X-ray chest</u> and neck (anteroposterior and <u>lateral</u>) [[11]](/library/Od1IJf0)

* May identify <u>subglottic</u> narrowing ; on anteroposterior view (steeple sign)

* May show concurrent <u>lower airway</u> involvement [[12]](/library/35YSPp)

* CT chest and neck: usually performed for differential diagnoses or suspected underlying congenital abnormalities  [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[13]](/library/y71doR0)

* <u>Laryngoscopy</u>/<u>bronchoscopy</u>: may be performed for suspected foreign bodies or <u>atypical croup</u> [[8]](/library/OH1IqR0)





![Steeple sign](media/wff6a84ry8dy82qcp5n1h9jn.jpg)

Steeple sign




> [!TIP]
> The <u>steeple sign</u> is not specific to croup; it may also be present with <u>bacterial tracheitis</u>, <u>epiglottitis</u>, and noninfectious etiologies such as <u>thermal injuries</u> and <u>neoplasms</u>. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)




### <u>Laboratory studies</u>




* <u>Respiratory viral panel</u>

* Usually reserved for patients who do not respond to initial treatment [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)

* Most commonly shows <u>parainfluenza</u>; <u>coinfections</u> are common. [[5]](/library/_715oR0)

* <u>CBC</u>: may help distinguish between bacterial and viral infections [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)

* <u>Blood gas</u> [[14]](/library/A71RoR0)

* Indicated for severe respiratory symptoms, e.g., <u>signs of impending respiratory failure</u>

* May show <u>hypoxemia</u> and/or <u>CO<sub>2</sub> retention</u>

---

## Management

### Approach [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[10]](/library/MybMfw)[[11]](/library/Od1IJf0)




* Keep the patient calm and minimize <u>distress</u>. 

* Allow the patient to maintain a comfortable position (usually semi-upright). [[7]](/library/w71hLR0)

* Examine the child in the parent's lap. [[15]](/library/971NLR0)

* Avoid examining the throat as this may precipitate <u>airway obstruction</u>. [[7]](/library/w71hLR0)

* <u>Hypoxemia</u>/<u>signs of impending respiratory failure</u>: Initiate immediate stabilization (e.g., supplemental oxygenation, <u>intubation</u>).

* Perform a <u>croup severity assessment</u> to guide treatment; consider using a scoring system (e.g., <u>Westley croup score</u>).

* All patients: <u>dexamethasone</u> and <u>supportive care</u> as needed (e.g., <u>antipyretics</u>, <u>IV fluids</u>)

* Patients with moderate/<u>severe croup</u>: Add <u>nebulized</u> <u>racemic epinephrine</u>.

* Regularly reassess patients.  [[10]](/library/MybMfw)

* Admit patients with <u>admission criteria for croup</u>, e.g., <u>severe croup</u>, age < 6 months.





> [!WARNING]
> <u>Agitation</u> can worsen symptoms and precipitate complete <u>airway obstruction</u>; keep children calm and defer distressing procedures (e.g., IV placement) until facilities are in place for immediate <u>intubation</u> if required. [[16]](/library/C71qLR0)




> [!TIP]
> <u>Nebulized</u> <u>racemic epinephrine</u> rapidly relieves <u>symptoms of respiratory distress</u>. <u>Dexamethasone</u> provides longer symptom relief but takes up to 6 hours to reduce <u>airway</u> swelling. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)




> [!WARNING]
> Humidified air, both in the hospital and as a home remedy (e.g., steam inhalation), has been used to treat croup, but there is no evidence that it is effective. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[5]](/library/_715oR0)[[17]](/library/bs1HtR0)




### Immediate stabilization [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)




* Contact anesthesia or ENT early because children with croup have <u>difficult airways</u>.

* Initiate <u>respiratory support</u>.

* <u>Hypoxemia</u> (e.g., <u>pulse oximetry</u> < 92%) and/or <u>signs of respiratory distress</u>

* Start <u>supplemental oxygen</u> (typically humidified).

* Consider modifications to <u>oxygen delivery</u> to prevent worsening <u>agitation</u>.  [[7]](/library/w71hLR0)[[18]](/library/x71ELR0)

* <u>Respiratory failure</u> or <u>signs of impending respiratory failure</u> [[12]](/library/35YSPp)

* <u>Endotracheal intubation</u> is required.

* Bring the <u>difficult airway cart</u> to the bedside.

* The most experienced physician should perform the <u>intubation</u>.





> [!WARNING]
> Individuals with croup have <u>difficult airways</u> due to <u>glottic</u> and <u>subglottic stenosis</u>; if <u>intubation</u> is needed, notify anesthesia or ENT as early as possible. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)




> [!TIP]
> Evidence on the <u>efficacy</u> of helium-oxygen (<u>heliox</u>) mixtures in croup is mixed; routine use is not recommended. [[19]](/library/B71zLR0)




### Croup severity assessment




* Follow local or institutional protocols where available.

* Croup scoring systems are susceptible to interobserver variability. [[20]](/library/z71roR0)

* The most commonly used score is the <u>Westley croup score</u>.   [[20]](/library/z71roR0)





| <br>Westley croup score [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[21]](/library/Tl16wS0)<br> |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical features |  | Score |
| <u>Level of consciousness</u> | Normal | 0 |
| Disoriented | 5 |  |
| <u>Cyanosis</u> | None | 0 |
| With <u>agitation</u><br> | 4 |  |
| At rest | 5 |  |
| <u>Stridor</u> | None | 0 |
| With <u>agitation</u><br> | 1 |  |
| At rest | 2 |  |
| Air entry | Normal | 0 |
| Decreased | 1 |  |
| Markedly decreased | 2 |  |
| <u>Retractions</u> | None | 0 |
| Mild | 1 |  |
| Moderate | 2 |  |
| Severe | 3 |  |
| <br>Interpretation <br><br>* ≥ 12 points: <u>impending respiratory failure</u><br><br>* 8–11 points: <u>severe croup</u><br><br>* 3–7 points: <u>moderate croup</u><br><br>* ≤ 2 points: <u>mild croup</u><br><br><br><br> |  |  |





> [!TIP]
> Over 80% of croup cases are mild. [[22]](/library/4l13CS0)




![Westley Croup Score](media/eb06iqpbtwgmu5mye9ruh175.jpg)

Westley Croup Score




### Treatment




* Give <u>dexamethasone</u> (<u>off-label</u>). DOSAGE  [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[23]](/library/Jd1sIf0)

* Reduces <u>airway</u> swelling within 6 hours

* Effects last up to 72 hours.

* Start <u>supportive care</u>. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[22]](/library/4l13CS0)

* Ensure recommended daily fluid intake (oral or IV).

* Offer <u>antipyretics</u> if <u>febrile</u>.

* Educate the family on concerning features, e.g., <u>signs of respiratory distress</u>, <u>signs of significant dehydration</u>.

* <u>Moderate croup</u>/<u>severe croup</u>: Add <u>nebulized epinephrine</u>. [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[12]](/library/35YSPp)

* Preferred: racemic epinephrine DOSAGE [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[12]](/library/35YSPp)

* Reduces <u>airway</u> swelling within 30 minutes

* Monitor for 2–4 hours for return of symptoms.  [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)[[11]](/library/Od1IJf0)

* Dose may be repeated as needed.

* Alternative: L-<u>epinephrine</u> DOSAGE [[3]](/library/pd1LIf0)





> [!TIP]
> Suspect other <u>causes of stridor</u> if there are no symptoms of an <u>upper respiratory infection</u> and if symptoms do not respond to treatments for croup.




### Disposition




* Discharge home with <u>return precautions</u> can be considered in the following cases:

* <u>Mild croup</u>

* <u>Moderate croup</u> that has responded to a single <u>nebulized epinephrine</u> treatment

* Patients with <u>severe croup</u> or other <u>risk factors</u> should be admitted; consider <u>pediatric ICU</u>.





#### Admission criteria for croup [[10]](/library/MybMfw)[[12]](/library/35YSPp)




* <u>Severe croup</u>

* Need for oxygen or <u>IV fluids</u>

* > 1 treatment with <u>nebulized epinephrine</u>

* Age < 6 months

* Persistent <u>tachypnea</u> or <u>tachycardia</u>

* Complex <u>medical history</u> (congenital cardiac or pulmonary disease, <u>premature birth</u>)

---

## Complications

* <u>Respiratory failure</u> (rare)

* <u>Pulmonary edema</u>

* <u>Pneumothorax</u>

* <u>Pneumomediastinum</u>

* Secondary bacterial infection (e.g., <u>bacterial tracheitis</u>)

* <u>Cardiac arrest</u> and <u>death</u>




We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.
